title: Whole Life Insurance Remittance Processing Rules: Applying, Returning and Refunding Premium Payments
content:
Money received on an Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance policy is applied as premium only as follows.

1. **Status.** A payment is applied as premium only while the policy status is applied, in force or in the grace period, as the system record for that policy shows.
2. **Order of application.** A remittance not designated as a loan repayment is applied first to the oldest unpaid installment, one installment per payment record. A remittance designated as a loan repayment is never applied to premium.
3. **Shortfalls.** A shortfall up to the premium shortage tolerance is accepted as full payment; a larger shortfall is not applied and is returned.
4. **Overpayments.** Unapplied money above the overpayment refund threshold is refunded; money at or below it is held toward the next installment.
5. **Dividend and conversion credits.** A dividend under the reduce-premium option and a conversion credit are applied to the next installment due, like a remittance.
6. **Returned payments.** A payment returned unpaid by the bank reverses only that payment, once; the installment becomes due again, and its grace period is counted from its original due date.
7. **EFT privilege.** The returned EFT count is the number of payments on the policy returned unpaid whose payment method was EFT, counted over the rolling 12 calendar months ending on the date of the return being evaluated, both ends included, the return being evaluated included. When that count reaches the tier's returned-draft limit, the monthly EFT privilege ends, the mode changes to quarterly direct billing from the next installment, and EFT may be elected again only the tier's re-enrollment wait in calendar months after that return.

## Status and application

| Policy status on the record | Payment applied as premium |
|---|---|
| Applied | Yes |
| In force | Yes |
| Grace period | Yes |

## Worked cases (hypothetical, returned-draft limit of 2, re-enrollment wait of 6 months)

- EFT drafts returned on February 10 and on the following January 25: the window for the January 25 return runs back 12 calendar months, so it includes February 10; the count is 2 and the privilege ends; the next installment is billed quarterly, and EFT may be elected again from July 25.
- EFT drafts returned on February 10 and on the following March 15: the February 10 return lies outside the 12 months ending March 15; the count for March 15 is 1.
- Two unpaid installments due April 1 and May 1 and one undesignated remittance: it is applied to the April 1 installment.
